identity_notes: As flagged by the partition brief, L-valine retrieval in this scope is overwhelmingly NOT about oral L-valine supplementation. The single largest category (~40 records) is metabolomics/biomarker systematic reviews and Mendelian-randomization studies across dozens of diseases (cancer, diabetes, hypertension, stroke, periodontal disease, etc.) where circulating valine/BCAA levels are measured as a biomarker, never administered -- all rejected as not_intervention. A second large category (~20 records) are complete false keyword matches: 'Val' as a genetic polymorphism position (BDNF Val66Met, COMT Val158Met), drug names containing 'val' (valganciclovir, valbenazine, patisiran), or valine as an incidental amino acid in an unrelated protein/peptide sequence or industrial-biotech context -- all rejected as off_topic. A third category (~15 records) are inborn errors of valine/BCAA metabolism (maple syrup urine disease, HIBADH deficiency, methylmalonic acidemia) where the clinical need is valine RESTRICTION, the opposite of supplementation. A fourth category is animal/agricultural feeding studies (pigs, cattle, goats, sheep, quail) -- rejected as animal_or_invitro. Among the genuinely relevant human oral-supplementation records that remain (~13), NONE test L-valine alone: every kept record delivers valine only as part of a branched-chain amino acid (BCAA) mixture (typically a 2:1:1 leucine:isoleucine:valine ratio) or a broader amino acid blend, so label_material_match is related_form_differs throughout and no record can isolate an L-valine-specific effect from the leucine/isoleucine co-ingredients. The best-supported BCAA-combination signal is for exercise-induced muscle damage markers (34612716, meta-analysis) and post-operative infection/ascites in oncological surgery (33648360, meta-analysis), both mixed/oral route findings for the BCAA combination, not valine specifically. No qualifying evidence exists in this scope for a standalone, isolated L-valine supplement matching a typical single-ingredient label.
